_README: Slots for the CROSS-ROUTE probe (scripts/cross_route.py, slurm/10_cross_route.sbatch).
THE ROUTE. The question is asked in language L; the answer is always FRENCH, the language
the facts were learned in. Skow et al. (arXiv 2609.40286, Table 2A) find learning transfers
strongly when only the QUESTION changes language (+0.47) and barely when the answer must
change too (+0.09) -- our 09 native-route probe hit the weak case. This tests the strong one.
EVERY SLOT NAMES ONE FRENCH TARGET, which must occur exactly once in the French gold answer
of the standalone forget01_fr config (pass 2 -- the wording LEARN and every UNLEARN arm
trained on). The prompt is the L question + the French answer cut just before the target.
No per-language spelling is needed, so slots are cheap to add.
TYPE is the axis the supervisor's hypothesis turns on:
common  -- a concept that must be TRANSLATED between languages (occupation, genre)
proper  -- a string carried ACROSS languages as-is or transliterated (name, award,
number  -- a date, kept separate because it is neither
